family_decisions.alternatives: Generated module-level wrappers cover _StatsProperty statistics, not trim_relative. The same trim behavior is not implemented as a second module-level alias.

family_decisions.alternatives: atomic_save only constructs AtomicSaver; the question begins at context exit. The Unix branch is the legitimate helper alternative region; Windows same-named functions are excluded by the explicit task condition.
family_decisions.component: This is successful file publication ordering and non-overwrite semantics. It is not a task on copied file-tree recipes or set_cloexec alone. AtomicSaver and its helper stages form one component.
family_decisions.gold_completeness: The complete __exit__ primary includes flush/fsync/close and the actual helper call. The complete Unix atomic_rename definition supplies hard-link publication and temporary-name removal. Surrounding platform branch was independently read; a span-only helper binding prevents conflation with same-named Windows definitions.
family_decisions.negative: Unix replace is plausible as another rename/publication helper. It directly calls os.rename, allowing replacement, and has neither the non-overwrite hard-link path nor AtomicSaver's flush/fsync/close sequence.
family_decisions.source_semantics: On successful AtomicSaver context exit, buffered writes are flushed, fsynced and the part file is closed before atomic_rename is called. In the non-Windows branch with overwrite=False, atomic_rename uses os.link then os.unlink, refusing an existing destination through link semantics.
family_decisions.variants: All variants retain Unix and non-overwriting successful save completion. The paraphrases state the concrete hard-link publication and temporary-name removal already implemented in that specified branch. They do not assert crash durability beyond the shown calls.

'Original member value' describes the returned attribute not being transformed by warning behavior, not immutability against subsequent unrelated user mutation.
